atlas-cn.0107: In 2025 Chengdu’s financial industry added 240.52 billion yuan and its information transmission, software and IT services 213.61 billion, up 9.6%.
atlas-cn.0108: Huawei gives its headquarters as Huawei Base, Bantian, Longgang District, Shenzhen, and says it has approximately 213,000 employees in more than 170 countries and regions, 100% privately owned by employees.
atlas-cn.0109: In 2025 the average annual wage in urban non-private units was 248,752 yuan in information transmission, software and IT services and 211,164 in finance, against 129,441 across all sectors and 113,594 in manufacturing; averages for all ages, not entry pay.
atlas-cn.0110: In the first half of 2026 the surveyed urban unemployment rate averaged 5.2% (5.0% in June) and 5.1% in the 31 large cities; for ages 30 to 59 it averaged 4.1%.
atlas-cn.0111: Chinese-language CVs are expected for local employers; bilingual CVs are recommended for joint ventures, wholly foreign-owned firms and multinationals, and English counts as an asset mainly for international or overseas-facing roles.
atlas-cn.0112: Campus hiring has two peaks: autumn recruitment from September to November or December, the main one, with tech firms opening an early batch in June or July and most offers made in November and December; and a smaller spring round from February or March to April or May.
atlas-cn.0113: Huawei announced its graduate drive for the class of 2026 on 15 August 2025 and its internship drive for the class of 2027 on 15 March 2026; its 2025 cycle started on 14 August 2024 and 15 March 2024.
atlas-cn.0114: The four big state banks (ICBC, CCB, ABC and Bank of China) plan to hire about 64,000 graduates in the 2026 campus round, down from 71,500 a year earlier and 77,600 in 2024, and want graduates who combine technology and banking.
atlas-cn.0115: A record 12.7 million students graduated in 2026, and unemployment among 16-to-24-year-olds outside school reached 18.9% in August 2026, the peak month when graduates enter the market.
atlas-cn.0116: The average annual wage in China’s urban non-private units was 129,441 yuan in 2025, up 4.3% (about 10,800 yuan a month); Shenzhen’s was 191,367 yuan, Guangzhou’s 166,790, Chengdu’s 131,874 and Suzhou’s 146,353.
atlas-cn.0117: Chinese graduates are hired in two campus seasons: the autumn drive (qiūzhāo), from September to November or December, with tech firms opening an early batch in June or July, and a smaller spring round (chūnzhāo) from February or March to April or May. Large firms run their own campaigns, and the national civil-service examination offered 38,100 central posts for 2026, about 26,000 of them reserved for fresh graduates.
atlas-cn.0118: Personal referrals and face-to-face networking remain powerful in China, and guanxi (personal ties) can decide who is hired, above all in state-owned firms and smaller companies.
atlas-cn.0120: Autumn recruitment is the main drive: roughly September to November or December, when most graduate roles are advertised and filled. Tech firms open an early batch (tíqiánpī) in June or July, and the peak for large tech, consumer-goods, pharma and Big Four employers runs from August to October.
atlas-cn.0121: Most offers go out in November and December, with a supplementary round (bǔlù) in December alongside the first spring openings. Spring recruitment, usually March to April, fills what is left.
atlas-cn.0122: Huawei shows the rhythm: its graduate drive for the class of 2026 was announced on 15 August 2025, and its internship drive for the class of 2027 on 15 March 2026.
atlas-cn.0123: Whether a candidate counts as a fresh graduate (yīngjièshēng) is decided by the employer, and returnees generally hold no tripartite agreement (sānfāng xiéyì) with a school.
atlas-cn.0124: Overseas-graduate fairs and the two-year campus window
atlas-cn.0125: Overseas graduates can attend the campus recruitment of Chinese universities for two years after graduating. The Ministry of Education’s CSCSE ran a China Talent Job Fair at the University of Nottingham in 2025, with 13 universities, institutes and companies, among them Peking University, Tsinghua, CRRC and Sinopec Engineering Construction.
atlas-cn.0126: Timing can clash: Chinese employers often want the degree certificate before signing a formal contract, so a one-year master’s awarded in winter misses a summer start. Manchester suggests applying a year later, starting on an internship contract or delaying onboarding.
atlas-cn.0127: Internship drives run ahead of the graduate drives: Huawei opened its internship intake on 15 March in 2024 and 2026 and on 17 March in 2025, and its graduate intake in mid-August. Shixiseng (shíxísēng) describes itself as a platform for internships and campus jobs.
atlas-cn.0128: Edinburgh advises doing internships while applying if a graduate job is hard to secure. A student on a study visa needs the school’s consent and a note on the residence permit before starting one.
atlas-cn.0130: The national civil-service exam offered 38,100 central posts for 2026: registration ran from 15 to 24 October 2025 and the written test was held on 30 November. About 26,000 posts were reserved for fresh graduates and more than 28,000 are at county level or below; the age limit is 38, or 43 for 2026 master’s and doctoral graduates.
atlas-cn.0131: State-owned companies use aptitude tests and HR-led interviews; they value loyalty and promotion is slow. The four big state banks plan about 64,000 graduate hires for 2026.
atlas-cn.0133: Zhaopin, Liepin, 51job and BOSS Zhipin carry internship, graduate and experienced roles; Liepin targets the middle-to-high-end market and BOSS Zhipin lets candidates talk to employers directly.
atlas-cn.0134: Private companies have more flexibility and often hire when a need arises, preferring candidates who can start at once.
atlas-cn.0136: Personal referrals and face-to-face networking remain powerful, and local networks and agencies complement online platforms. WeChat official accounts and recruitment group chats, and campus posts on Xiaohongshu, carry recruiting news and informal coffee chats.
atlas-cn.0137: Agencies and headhunters for experienced hires
atlas-cn.0138: HiredChina is a portal for international talent, with language support and filters for specialised expertise. Job changers typically expect a 10% to 20% rise over their current package, and counteroffers and non-competition agreements can stop a move.
atlas-cn.0139: A record 12.7 million students graduated in 2026, and unemployment among 16-to-24-year-olds outside school reached 18.9% in August 2026, the peak season when graduates enter the market.
atlas-cn.0140: The big banks are hiring fewer: openings fall each year while the six large state banks cut more than 30,000 employees in the first half of 2026.
atlas-cn.0141: The four big state banks still hire graduates in tens of thousands through autumn campus recruitment, but fewer each year: about 64,000 planned for 2026 against 71,500 a year earlier and 77,600 in 2024, with strong demand for graduates who combine finance and technology.
atlas-cn.0142: The Big Four recruit in the same autumn peak as other large employers, from August to October. In September 2024 Chinese authorities suspended PwC’s mainland audit arm, PwC ZhongTian, for six months over its Evergrande audit.
atlas-cn.0143: Public-sector graduate hiring runs through the national civil-service exam and state-owned firms: 38,100 central posts for 2026, with about 26,000 reserved for fresh graduates.
atlas-cn.0144: Tech groups recruit thousands of graduates a year through autumn campus campaigns; ByteDance offered 5,000 places for 2026, with research and development roles up 23%. Tsinghua, Peking, Zhejiang and Shanghai Jiao Tong are the usual sources.
atlas-cn.0145: Banks and tech groups compete for graduates who combine finance or business with AI and data skills, the one area where campus demand is rising. China Merchants Bank, for one, is hiring AI research and development staff who know banking.
atlas-cn.0146: The labels 985 and 211 are still commonly used in mainland China to refer to top universities; project 985 selected 39 of them. A UK careers service advises putting your university’s and programme’s ranking on the CV, because Chinese employers may not know foreign institutions.
atlas-cn.0147: Employers recruit on named campuses: the CSCSE job fair in Nottingham drew Peking University and Tsinghua.
atlas-cn.0148: The Ministry of Education’s graduate platform (ncss.cn) runs dedicated employer events and joint recruitment events, and links to provincial and school sites. Huawei lists an Open Day, a competition and online information sessions for its campus drives.
atlas-cn.0149: For graduates of foreign universities, the CSCSE job fairs held abroad, such as the one at Nottingham in 2025, bring Chinese universities, institutes and state companies to the students.
atlas-cn.0150: Two peaks: autumn (September to November or December), the main one, and spring (February to May). Vacancies appear year-round, and some firms recruit in December and January.
atlas-cn.0151: The fresh-graduate work-permit route for foreigners asks for a master’s or above, from a Chinese or a well-known overseas university. Research, algorithm and R&D roles in tech and banking tend to ask for postgraduate degrees, but no page we read gives a share.
atlas-cn.0152: Foreign degrees are verified by the CSCSE, which operates under the Ministry of Education; the online application takes 10 to 20 working days to review. Many employers use the CSCSE system to verify candidates’ overseas qualifications.
atlas-cn.0153: The 985 and 211 labels remain the shorthand for top universities, and a UK careers service tells applicants to state their university’s ranking because employers may not know it. Top campuses are where recruiters go.
atlas-cn.0154: Degree graduates reach employers through campus recruiting and internships; apprenticeship and dual-study contracts are not a route we found in any source for university graduates.
